TOPSIS Relative-Entropy Centrality

Source: R/centrality-batch63.R
centrality_topsis_re.Rd

The multi-attribute ranking method of Liu et al. (2015), TOPSIS-RE, rates every node on four indicators, degree centrality, closeness centrality, betweenness centrality and the improved k-shell index, and scores it by how close it lies to the best value of each and how far from the worst. Each indicator is divided by its Euclidean norm over the nodes and multiplied by its weight, 0.0625, 0.1875, 0.1875 and 0.5625 in that order, to give \(r_{ij}\). With \(r_j^+\) and \(r_j^-\) the largest and the smallest value of indicator \(j\), $$S_i^{+} = \Bigl\{\sum_{j} \Bigl[r_j^{+} \log\frac{r_j^{+}}{r_{ij}} + (1 - r_j^{+}) \log\frac{1 - r_j^{+}}{1 - r_{ij}}\Bigr]\Bigr\}^{1/2}, \qquad C_i = \frac{S_i^{-}}{S_i^{+} + S_i^{-}},$$ and \(S_i^-\) is defined in the same way with \(r_j^-\).

Usage

centrality_topsis_re(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality.

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order, between 0 and 1, or NA at every node when the score is undefined.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. The score runs from 0 to 1, and a node that is best on all four indicators scores 1. The weights are those the source derives and prints; they are part of the method.

A node with an indicator equal to zero while another node has a positive value scores 0, because its distance from the best is then infinite. Betweenness is zero for every node with a single tie, so all such nodes score 0. The equation of the source gives this result, but the source does not discuss it, and a figure in it shows positive scores for such nodes without saying how they were obtained.

The measure needs a connected network of at least two nodes whose nodes are not all alike. Otherwise every score is NA with a cograph_undefined_measure warning.

References

Liu, Z., Jiang, C., Wang, J. and Yu, H. (2015). The node importance in actual complex networks based on a multi-attribute ranking method. Knowledge-Based Systems, 84, 56-66. doi:10.1016/j.knosys.2015.03.026 .

See also

centrality_iksd, centrality_hybrid, centrality.

Examples

kite <- matrix(0, 6, 6, dimnames = list(letters[1:6], letters[1:6]))
kite[rbind(c(1, 2), c(1, 3), c(2, 3), c(3, 4), c(4, 5), c(4, 6))] <- 1
kite <- kite + t(kite)
centrality_topsis_re(kite)
#>         a         b         c         d         e         f 
#> 0.0000000 0.0000000 0.9226135 0.7338031 0.0000000 0.0000000
